our mission.

Teach one billion people how to breathe.

Are you in?

Breathing is the one thing every human on Earth shares. It doesn’t matter your age, your passport, your title or your bank account. If you’re alive, you breathe, and the way you breathe shapes how you live. People of the Prana exists to teach the world to do it well.

Start with the free app Read Esther’s story

imagine this.

What would the world look like if slow breathing were the new baseline?

Have you ever been around someone who breathes slowly? They feel really good to be around. Your shoulders drop, your voice softens and, without even trying, you start to breathe a little slower too.

Now imagine that was normal. The nurse who slows her breath before she walks into the next room. The teacher who breathes with her class before a test. The manager who takes three breaths before the hard conversation, and the parent who does the same at bedtime. Hospitals, schools and workplaces where calm is the baseline, not the exception.

That’s the world we’re building, one breath at a time.

Breathing well belongs everywhere

  • Therapy rooms
  • Hospitals
  • Classrooms
  • Boardrooms
  • Ambulances
  • Kitchens
  • Forests
  • Zoom calls
  • Bedrooms at 3 a.m.

those who breathe together, stay together.

Breathing is contagious.

Our nervous systems are always reading each other: the breath, the pace of a voice, the stillness or tension in a body. When one person in the room breathes slowly, everyone else gets permission to follow. Stress spreads this way. So does calm. That’s why we teach breathing in groups, in families and in teams, and why we hope you’ll pass it on.

shut up & breathe.

Life took away my voice so I could finally hear.

Growing up, I never paid attention to my breath. I only noticed it when I couldn’t breathe well. After my third surgery for thyroid cancer, I lost my voice for about six months, while I was working and raising two small children. The only thing I could do was shut up and breathe.

So I began practicing every morning before dawn, and in that silence I learned how to listen. For ten years I studied with my teacher, who taught in the traditional way, through silence and presence. I didn’t understand what was happening, but I knew it felt like peace, and like remembering something true.

Then the pandemic hit, and the whole world went into a full blown panic attack. People simply were not breathing. And I was calm. That’s when I understood why I had been given these practices. I started teaching free classes on Zoom with a terrible camera and bad lighting, and about 30 people showed up, twice a week, breathing together in the dark. Years later, many of them told me those classes were their lifeline.

The group that kept coming became the People of the Prana.

What is prana?

Prana is life force energy: the stuff that makes us truly alive, creative and full of vitality. And vitality is the antidote to stress. When your life force is high, stress bounces off you. Prana is all around us, all the time. All we have to do is learn to receive it, and the breath is how.

my story.

I see so many people on the edge of burnout, doing the most important work in the world.

Health care workers, mental health workers, first responders, teachers: people in demanding jobs who show up for everyone else. I know that world from the inside. I have worked in it for 20 years as a psychotherapist, much of that time with highly traumatized clients. I know the high pressure and the long hours, and I know the genuine desire to serve vulnerable people from a place of love and care. I also know how easy it is, in the middle of all that giving, to forget to take care of ourselves.

In all the training programs I have come across, I have never seen an emphasis on caring for our own mental health as practitioners, or on anything that strengthens the nervous system. If anything, it’s the opposite: push through, stay late, take care of yourself later. That mentality is not sustainable. Every year, young professionals enter these fields not knowing how they will keep up. That is the reality.

There is never enough time. But breathing takes almost none, and it goes everywhere you go. When you can stay calm in a difficult situation, you can actually do your job better, and you feel better doing it.

My own daily practice is what kept me steady while colleagues around me went in and out of burnout. I want every helper to have that.

Esther Kalaba, MA, RP

Who are the People of the Prana?

A psychotherapist and a composer, who believe the world would work much better if more people breathed better.

Esther Kalaba, MA, RP, AT

Co-founder. Psychotherapist, art therapist and breath teacher.

I’m a registered psychotherapist and art therapist, licensed in Ontario and Quebec, a trained medical herbalist and a Kundalini yoga teacher. For 20 years I’ve blended psychotherapy, somatics, breathwork, art, sound and nervous system science into an approach that is practical, creative and deeply human. My gift is translating complex healing into simple tools anyone can use, in real life, on real days, in real moments of “I cannot do this anymore.” I’m also the founder of The SEED Lodge, our retreat centre near Georgian Bay.

Ma’amo Koba

Co-founder. Composer and producer.

I’m a Grammy nominated composer and producer, a Juno and ADISQ winner, with credits for NASA, HBO and Apple, and the founder of Tree Mountain Studios. My work focuses on the physics of sound and its direct effect on the body: functional music designed to steady the breath and regulate the nervous system. I created the music behind BEAT + BREATH™.
